citation.title: 3D field phase-space control in tokamak plasmas
citation.authors: Park, J.-K.; Jeon, Y.; In, Y.; Ahn, J.-W.; Nazikian, R.; Park, G.; Kim, J.; Lee, H.; Ko, W.; Kim, H.-S.; Logan, N. C.; Wang, Z.; Feibush, E. A.; Menard, J. E.; Zarnstorff, M. C.

topic: Ideal plasma-response (IPEC) modeling of n=1/n=2 RMP coil phase space for ELM suppression without locked modes in KSTAR
own_question: Which 3D coil configurations give ELM suppression without core locked-mode disruption?
actual_method_and_evidence: IPEC resonant-field metrics for core and edge. Thresholds were calibrated at single empirical operating points. Predictions were compared with KSTAR coil-ramp discharges. Ti came from carbon CX emission with two-Gaussian fitting and is used only as a context trace. The paper contains no CES nowcasting, no BES/ECEI inference and no timing analysis.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: KSTAR H-mode studies report ion temperature inferred from carbon charge-exchange emission. This is impurity Ti and not main-ion Ti.
claim_checks.qualification: Context only. This is not a pedestal-top chord nowcast, and the source does not discuss latency.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not applicable. The source does not address report arrival timing or causal inputs.
validation_if_relevant: Experimental checks of predicted coil windows on selected discharges. These do not form a held-out data split.
forbidden_inferences: This paper does not support the need for, or the feasibility of, real-time CES nowcasting.
It provides no evidence on the value of BES/ECEI for temperature estimation.
Its carbon CX Ti is not main-ion temperature or independent truth.
It should not be cited as KSTAR2022 data.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Exclude, or at most cite as optional application context, for example RMP/ELM control in KSTAR. It does not bear on the nowcasting question.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
